description: Morris's 2014 algorithm decides *dynamic controllability* of a simple temporal network with uncertainty (STNU) in `O(n³)` time. A *negative node* is a point with a negative incoming edge. From each negative node, the algorithm runs Dijkstra's algorithm backwards through non-negative edges, and each path that reaches distance zero or more becomes a new ordinary edge. When the search meets another negative node, it processes that node first; if that node is still in progress, the nested paths form a negative cycle and the network is not controllable. `temporal-control` uses it as its default checker, and its dispatchable variant also keeps the derived edges and *waits* ("execute only after a delay, unless this duration has ended").

papers.title: Dynamic Controllability and Dispatchability Relationships
papers.venue: CPAIOR 2014, Lecture Notes in Computer Science

papers.authors: Nikhil Bhargava, Tiago Vaquero, Brian Williams
papers.title: Faster Conflict Generation for Dynamic Controllability
